chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Nuʿaym al-Qābūsī, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, that he said:

Indeed, my son ʿAlī is the eldest of my children, the most dutiful of them in my sight, and the most beloved of them to me; and he looks with me into al-Jafr, and none has looked into it except a Prophet or the successor of a Prophet.

key_terms.أَبَرُّهُمْ: the most dutiful or righteous among them; indicating superior virtue
key_terms.أَحَبُّهُمْ: the most beloved among them; indicating special closeness
key_terms.أَكْبَرُ: the eldest; indicating seniority among the children
key_terms.ابْنِي: my son; identifying the Imam’s filial relationship
key_terms.الْجَفْرِ: al-Jafr; a sacred repository of special knowledge in this context
key_terms.عَلِيًّا: ʿAlī; the son being designated and praised in the narration
key_terms.نَبِيٌّ: a Prophet; one of the only categories said to look into it
key_terms.وَصِيُّ: successor; the designated heir of a Prophet in this context

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith indicate about Imam ʿAlī al-Riḍā’s special status and access to al-Jafr?
ai.summary: This hadith states the special rank of Imam ʿAlī among the children of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, describing him as the eldest, the most dutiful, and the most beloved. It also links him to al-Jafr, indicating a privileged access associated only with a Prophet or the successor of a Prophet, and thus points to his distinctive religious authority.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muawiya Bin Hukeym, from Nuaym Al Qabousy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘My<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> Ali<sup>asws</sup> is the eldest of my<sup>asws</sup> children, and the more righteous of them in my<sup>asws</sup> presence, and the most beloved of them to me<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> looks into Al-Jaf’r with me<sup>asws</sup>, and none looks into it except for a Prophet<sup>as</sup> or a successor<sup>as</sup> of a Prophet<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu‘awiya ibn Hakim from Nu‘aym al-Qabusi from abu al-Hassan (a.s.) who has said the following.

“My son, Ali is the eldest of my sons and the most virtuous among them to me and the most beloved of them to me. He looks into the Jafr (a secret source of knowledge) with me. No one looks into it except a prophet or the executor of the will of a prophet.”
